To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a novel framework for capsule networks, (2) our framework is provably equivariant, (3) we propose a new routing mechanism for capsule networks based on degree centrality, (4) our framework is more robust to transformations and performs better than several baselines.

(i) the SOV of capsules of successive layers can be learnt in an efficient and equivariant fashion, and (ii) this can be used to improve the performance and equivariance properties of capsule networks.

(i) the choice of prediction network and the routing mechanism in capsule networks is crucial to the preservation of equivariance, and (ii) learning to projectively encode SOVs for capsules of successive layers, and using equivariant functions to project between them, leads to better equivariance and hence better performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing equivariant capsule networks that are both theoretically sound, as well as practical.
developing a general framework for learning deep equivariant capsule networks, and also with a specific instantiation of it.
developing equivariant capsule networks that can better represent the compositional structure of the world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SOV framework is a generalisation of the capsule idea, which allows for a more principled, efficient, and theoretically sound implementation of capsule networks.
our model is a novel, theoretically sound, and practically efficient, instantiation of equivariant capsule networks.
the proposed model, in its current form, is a step in the right direction for building a more general, robust and scalable equivariant capsule network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a general framework for capsule networks, and have shown that this framework is indeed able to improve upon the state-of-the-art for capsule networks.
our proposed model is a step forward for equivariant learning in capsule networks, as well as in deep learning more broadly.

our model is a generalisation of the standard capsule network architecture that can be used for learning equivariant capsule networks, and is also a generalisation of equivariant convolutional architectures that can be used to learn capsule networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the equivariance properties of capsule networks can be significantly improved by a careful choice of prediction networks, and the routing mechanism.
learning the SOV is key to achieving equivariance and hence compositional representations in deep neural networks.
learning the space of variation of capsules, and the projection into them, can be used to build equivariant networks with provable guarantees.
